provenance: I authored the Unique formalization and its additional evaluation checks, but did not author Shared or the correspondence implementation. For this cross-layer review I read all required authored units, exact Lean selections and the review-policy snapshot; I also inspected the named definitions and statement assumptions in any additionally listed source context. I compared the Shared design independently, found and requested correction of a stored-mode/path-mode wording mismatch, then reread the changed shared.steps snapshot and verified other required inputs unchanged before deciding. Listing a containing source context records the inspected definitions, not an audit of every proof tactic in that file.
rationale: unit:shared.correspondence states both preservation of each Given step and reflection of every Shared successor of an embedded Given configuration. The selected step_correspondence theorem is an iff whose left side has arbitrary Shared after, and whose right side existentially supplies Unique successor with a Unique step and after=embedConfiguration successor. This exactly gives both listed directions without assuming the successor is already embedded. It quantifies over arbitrary classes/before/after and has no WF, reachability, or purity premise exposed to the caller; purity is supplied by the embedding internally. The dependencies given.steps/shared.steps define the two complete-expression statement judgments and shared.embedding defines E, including recursive constructors and tagged IDs. This proves the claimed one-step bisimulation of the embedded fragment, not equivalence for arbitrary Shared programs containing giveShare.
limitations: This comparison checks prose/notation and formal statement correspondence; it does not independently certify Lean proof checking or audit proof tactics.
